summary: An inactive direct reconstruction proves the classical connected-fiber factorization of every surjective holomorphic map from a connected compact complex manifold to a compact curve. Completing the covering of regular fiber components across punctures gives the intermediate curve, including ramification and scheme fiber multiplicities. The reviewed 648 metric therefore applies to every such curve map, without a separate factorization hypothesis.
proof_obligations: The finite critical-value argument is independent of fiber connectedness.
The proper-submersion component-cover proof applies locally on the punctured compact curve; compactness is used over closed local disks.
Regular fiber component counts are finite and locally constant, giving one finite degree d.
The complement of the analytic fiber divisor is connected, with a local complex-line path argument and a chain-of-balls global argument.
Connected finite covers of punctured disks have the form w to w^e by the half-plane universal cover and the index-e subgroup.
The punctured cover has finitely many ends over each missing value, whose degrees sum to d.
Adding one disk point at each end gives Hausdorff holomorphic charts and a finite proper compact completion.
A small coordinate-ball complement is connected, so its quotient image selects one punctured end.
The coordinate is bounded and satisfies its e-th-power identity; transverse one-variable extension and Hartogs extension justify filling singular divisors.
The extended quotient maps glue on the dense regular locus and are surjective by compactness and density.
Properness confines nearby fibers to disjoint neighborhoods of a hypothetical split special fiber.
Local one-variable restrictions make the quotient map open; nearby regular connected fibers exclude that split.
A finite disjoint union of connected compact quotient fibers is precisely the original fiber component decomposition.
Local ramification and quotient-fiber multiplicities multiply; neither reduced fibers nor unramified completion is assumed.
Every alternative factor is unramified over regular values, giving the same component cover; punctured-disk coordinates extend its unique isomorphism.
The factor supplies the exact hypothesis of 648; area dA proves negative-area emptiness and the zero-area singleton.
Rescaling the upstairs trace metric by d inverse preserves completeness, geodesics, closure and nearest retraction.
The original base pushforward still fails to separate; existence of a factor does not make all potentials descend to the original curve.

classical_foundations_used: Finite covering classification of a punctured disk, one-variable bounded holomorphic extension, codimension-two Hartogs extension and local reduced-divisor singular-locus codimension. The argument is a direct reconstruction of the curve case of classical Stein factorization; no novelty claim or general coherent-direct-image theorem adoption.
nearby_cases: Squared-coordinate map on P1 times P1: d=2, regular fibers have two components, branch fibers have one component with multiplicity two.
Connected map with multiple critical fibers: d=1, so the curve factor is the original base while quotient-fiber multiplicities remain.
Finite isogeny in the old submersion example: the factor is the unramified component covering.
Dimension one: the quotient is an isomorphism and the finite factor is the original finite map.
